To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Monte Carlo tree search is an RL algorithm; 2) Monte Carlo tree exploration is a form of Q-learning; 3) Monte Carlo tree policy evaluation is a form of temporal difference learning; 4) Monte Carlo tree evaluation is a form a value function learning; 5) Monte Carlo tree planning is a form of model learning.
Monte Carlo Tree Search can be seen as a form of Reinforcement Learning, and that this insight can be used to develop a new generation of search algorithms.

Monte Carlo Tree Search is a form of Reinforcement Learning and that the use of Reinforcement Learning in conjunction with Monte Carlo Tree Search leads to a new class of algorithms with encouraging results on several games and video games.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What can RL teach us about MCTS?
the following questions: (1) What is the relationship between MCTS and RL?
the question of how much of RL is needed in order to achieve state of the art results in games.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RL is to MCTS what MCTS is to alpha-beta search.
MCTS is to RL what RL is to MCTS.
MCTS is to RL what RL is to MCTS: a powerful tool to solve complex sequential decision making problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Monte Carlo tree search can be seen as a particular case of RL.
we show that RL is not just about the learning, but also about the planning and the search.
we are able to combine the advantages of planning and learning, and that we can learn from planning and search.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RL techniques can be used to enhance the search for the next action, and to improve the policy for the current state.
MCTS can be viewed as a specific instantiation of a general framework for online planning and learning, and that this view opens up new research directions and applications.
RL techniques can be applied to tree search in order to improve its efficiency.
